# Job Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 419v–420r

---

**1** "I am sick of my own life!
So I will hold nothing back — I will pour out my complaint;
I will speak from the depth of my bitterness.

**2** I will say to God, 'Don't just declare me guilty!
Tell me what the charges are. Tell me why you are fighting against me.'

**3** Does it give you pleasure to crush me?
Do you enjoy despising the work of your own hands
while smiling on the schemes of the wicked?

**4** Do you have human eyes?
Do you see things the way a mortal does?

**5** Is your life as short as mine?
Are your years as brief as a man's,

**6** that you have to hunt so urgently for my faults
and dig so hard to find my sin?

**7** You know perfectly well that I am not guilty —
yet no one can rescue me from your grip.

**8** Your own hands shaped me and formed me —
every part of me — and now you turn around and destroy me!

**9** Remember that you molded me like clay.
Are you going to turn me back to dust so soon?

**10** You poured me out like milk
and formed me like cheese setting in a mold.

**11** You dressed me in skin and flesh
and wove me together with bones and muscles.

**12** You gave me life and showed me unfailing love;
your watchful care kept me alive.

**13** But all along you had this hidden in your heart —
I know now this was your plan all along:

**14** to watch me and, the moment I sinned,
to refuse to let me off the hook.

**15** If I am wicked, I am doomed.
If I am righteous, I still cannot hold my head up —
I am drowning in shame, staring at my own misery.

**16** If I dare to stand tall, you hunt me like a lion
and unleash your terrifying power against me again.

**17** You send wave after wave of accusers against me;
your anger against me keeps growing.
I face fresh attacks, one after another.

**18** Why did you let me be born at all?
I wish I had died before anyone ever saw me.

**19** I wish I had never existed —
carried straight from the womb to the grave.

**20** My few remaining days are almost gone.
Can't you just stop? Leave me alone
so I can have one small moment of relief

**21** before I go to the place of no return —
the land of darkness and deepest shadow,

**22** a land of utter blackness,
of shadow and chaos,
where even the light is dark."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**God the artisan who smashes his own work (vv.8-12):** Job builds a devastating case: God is a potter who lovingly shapes clay, a cheesemaker who carefully curdles milk, a weaver who knits bone and sinew — and then destroys what he made. The intimacy of the creation imagery makes the destruction feel like betrayal. This is not the complaint of a man who never knew God; it is the complaint of someone who was loved and cannot understand why the love has turned violent.

**"This was your plan all along" (v.13):** Job suspects divine premeditation — that God created him knowing he would eventually destroy him. This is, ironically, closer to the truth revealed in the prologue than anything the friends say. God did agree to the Adversary's test. But the reader knows what Job does not: the purpose was not destruction but vindication.

**"Where even the light is dark" (v.22):** This closing line is one of the most extraordinary in all of poetry. Four words for darkness pile up, and then the final paradox: what passes for light in that place is itself darkness. It is a description of a world where the fundamental distinction of Genesis 1 — light separated from darkness — has been undone.

---
*— PNEUMA*
